title: cutover-microsprint-checklist
body:
Purpose: quick, personal cutover checklist for small/medium releases (microsprints). Not the official runbook — condensed operator notes + reminders + escape hatches.

TL;DR timeline (T-):
- T-72h: freeze PRs touching serving runtime config; ensure changelog entry; flag any backports.
- T-24h: dry-run of deploy on staging with identical scale. Collect perf numbers.
- T-2h: final smoke tests on staging; create rollback plan and record current leader commit hashes.
- T-15m: Slack 'release-imminent' to #release-ops and affected product channels.
- T: deploy to prod (canary first), watch 30m, promote if green.
- T+1h: start degraded-load ramp; T+4h: finalize post-release notes.

Quick items to capture before kick:
- Active PRs to include: PR#3421 (platform), PR#3419 (console). Confirm CI green.
- Backports required: serving runtime perf fix -> create branch release/1.4.2-backport. Patch list:
  - file: runtime/kv_cache.c (cherry-pick ab34f2)
  - file: ops/route_policy.go (cherry-pick c3d1aa)
- Docs: update /docs/release-notes/1.4.2.md after deploy.

Environment & artifacts (where to look quickly):
- Current prod leader commit: commit: a7b9f3d (master).
- Staging S3 logs: s3://redwood-logs/staging/2025-11-02/
- Prod S3 logs (last 24h): s3://redwood-logs/prod/2025-11-06/
- Canary dashboards: Console > Deployments > release-1-4-2 > Canary
- Perf script (run locally): scripts/run_perf.sh --target staging --cpus 16

Commands I run during cutover (copy/paste):
- Deploy canary: redwood deploy --env prod --version v1.4.2 --canary 10% --timeout 10m
- Promote: redwood promote --env prod --from canary --to stable
- Rollback (fast): redwood rollback --env prod --to-commit a7b9f3d
- Health check tail: kubectl -n redwood logs -l app=runtime --since=10m | grep -E "ERROR|WARN"

Canary checklist (first 30m):
- [ ] Health endpoints green across 3 zones
- [ ] 95p latency within baseline +10%
- [ ] Error rate not increased >0.5% absolute
- [ ] No OOMs or GPU driver restarts in node logs
- [ ] Key customer routes exercised (simulate top-5 routes)

If anything fails: immediate actions
- If health endpoints fail: rollback to previous commit (use rollback command), notify #release-ops with short log snippet, escalate to on-call SRE.
- If latency regresses and error rate low: reduce traffic by halving canary and extend observation window to 60m; open a quick GH issue and attach perf traces.
- If GPU restarts: stop the deployment, collect /var/log/nvidia*, dump dmesg, and hand off to infra (tag: @infra-oncall).

Comms draft (post to #release-ops):
Title: "Release v1.4.2 — canary started"
Body: "Canary started at HH:MM UTC. Version: v1.4.2. Canary 10% across us-east-1/us-west-2/eu-west-1. Watching metrics: latency, errors, GPU restarts. If no issues by +30m, will promote. Contact: @Avery (pager)"

Personal quick reminders (note-to-self style):
- Bring laptop charger.
- Avoid big config merges during T-24h to T+4h window.
- If I step away, leave 'do not push' message in #release-ops.

Post-release quick audit (T+2h):
- [ ] Confirm rollout finished across all regions.
- [ ] Run smoke queries for top-10 customers.
- [ ] Check tracing for any new 5xx spikes.
- [ ] Upload prod perf snapshots to PR and attach during release note update.
- [ ] Mark release ticket REL-987 as DONE with short summary.

Postmortem triggers (notes for follow-up):
- Trigger full postmortem if:
  - outage > 5 minutes attributed to this release, or
  - rollback required after canary for unknown root cause, or
  - customer-facing SLA breach.
- Otherwise, short blameless incident note in ticket and link to perf graphs.

Open questions / TODOs (fill before next run):
- Need faster access to historical kernel crash logs in Console (ticket raised?).
- Consider adding a pre-deploy quick-kill toggle in routing layer to drop traffic to canary if needed.
- Validate that redwood promote command will respect autoscaler cooldowns (test on staging).

End-of-run checklist (T+24h):
- [ ] Close release ticket, link PRs and perf artifacts.
- [ ] Update changelog and release notes.
- [ ] Schedule 15m retro with Eng + SRE if any anomalies.
- [ ] Move any follow-up items into JIRA with owners and due dates.

Random operator tips (learned from past microsprints):
- Keep a small set of pre-coded queries handy that reproduce customer flows (saves time during investigation).
- If you see small error spikes that correlate with GC times, try bumping JVM flags for the specific worker pod as a stop-gap and open perf task.
- When in doubt, reduce traffic and extend the observation window — easier to be conservative.

Notes-to-self: breathe. prefer bullet notes during the run. Update this doc after the release so future microsprint runs are faster.
